title.narrative: BELA III (Defending Environmental Rights & Promoting Justice, 2024-2027)
BELA III (Defending Environmental Rights & Promoting Justice, 2024-2027)

description.narrative:
Outcome 1: Defended citizens rights to environment
BELA successfully ensured continued legal protection and advocacy for environmental justice through Public Interest Environmental Litigations (PIELs), filing new cases as well as following up on ongoing cases. Its efforts pressured public authorities and regulators towards stricter enforcement of protection laws and policy implementation. BELA promoted accountability and enhanced environmental governance by holding responsible parties answerable for their actions, such as local public development authorities who disregard environmental impact assessments (EIAs) and safeguards, and corporations who are polluters. Furthermore, BELAs initiatives led to increased compliance and operational efficiency among identified private sector actors, reinforcing sustainable business practices and responsible environmental management.
During the reporting period, BELA secured significant judgments on 3 PIELs which have previously been filed. The cases include safeguarding wetlands, agricultural lands, and holding developers accountable for unauthorized environmental damage.
During the reporting period, BELA successfully organized 20 community consultations in different districts, addressing a range of critical environmental and legal concerns. These sessions not only facilitated follow-ups on existing cases but also empowered community members to initiate new legal actions on issues related to Water Scarcity & Flooding, River & Wetland Encroachment & Pollution, Brick Kiln impacts on Agricultural Land, Illegal Hill Cutting & Landslides, Industrial Pollution, Unregulated Stone & Sand Extraction and Crushing, Deforestation & Indigenous Rights, and Human-wildlife conflict. Furthermore, a total of 21 Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) were conducted across 6 divisions - Barishal, Chattogram, Khulna, Rajshahi, Sylhet, and Mymensingh - to identify emerging environmental justice issues and assess community perspectives as part of informing about the state of environmental protection capacities in the country.
Another important legal instrument for environmental protection is the Right to Information (RTI) Act, with BELA serving a total of 113 RTI applications on 77 issues concerning environmental and land-related issues across various districts of Bangladesh. The applications sought information on topics such as pollution, encroachment, wetland and river protection, waste management, and forestry to be used for inspection reports, enforcement records, and legal actions taken against encroachers and polluters. RTI applications were also used to gather information on relevant government initiatives and lease agreements for rivers and quarries.
Outcome 2: Promoted compliance and advocated for environmental justice issues and greener production practices in the industrial sectors
This outcome is intended to challenge BELA to find ways to engage constructively with private sector actors who are crucial to reducing industrial pollution risks. During 2024, BELA focused specifically on the renewable energy (RE) space, co-organizing the 2nd Bangladesh Energy Prosperity 2050 Conference. This has resulted in constructive engagements with local and multinational energy suppliers and private financiers on joint policy advocacy for championing the transition to 100% renewable energy in Bangladesh. A number of concrete actions are expected to be implemented in the coming years as a result of these efforts.
Outcome 3: Engaged systematically with global movements and local citizens groups in environmental justice initiatives
BELA served as a technical expert supporting Bangladesh official negotiators in the Global Plastics Treaty, participating in the 5th session of the Intergovernmental Negotiating Committee (INC-5) in Busan, South Korea, alongside allies from Friends of the Earth International (FoEI) and the Global Alliance for Incinerator Alternatives (GAIA). It actively raised awareness and engagement among youth groups spearheading national campaigns and public demonstrations against plastic pollution.
BELA was invited by the Bangladesh's government delegation to be one of its technical advisors in the UN Biodiversity Convention (COP 16) negotiations in Cali, Colombia, where Bangladesh reported on progress in compliance to 23 targets for the Global Biodiversity Framework.
For the UN Conference of Parties (COP29) in Baku, Azerbaijan, BELA was invited to be part of the official country delegation, supporting the negotiations on the New Collective Quantified Goal on Climate Finance (NCQG), and coordinating with Least Developed Countries (LDC) groups and civil society partners of the Demand Climate Justice (DCJ) movement.
Outcome 4: Documented important facts and trends, informed opinions and disseminated knowledge on environmental justice issues
BELA primarily reported activities under this outcome. Through various research, publications, and training initiatives, BELA expects to raise awareness about critical environmental issues, foster development of the needed capacities among stakeholders about environmental risks and sustainable alternatives.
Outcome 5: Strengthened Organizational Capacity
The activities implemented during the reporting period are expected to produce results which the Embassy will verify as part of the next CoP. One area of progress is in relation to gender mainstreaming. Over the past year, BELA has strengthened its commitment to gender sensitivity by establishing the Disciplinary and Preventing Sexual Harassment, Exploitation, and Abuse (PSHEA) Committee dedicated to fostering a safe, inclusive, and gender-responsive work environment by addressing complaints of harassment, exploitation, and abuse with fairness and confidentiality. Beyond investigation and disciplinary measures, the committee plays a crucial role in shaping policies, guidelines, and awareness initiatives engaging all staff, interns, and volunteers, with plans to extend to network members.
